Now I understand the code. Let me reconsider the crash.

`map.sanitize(c, this, &(this+data))` calls `OffsetTo::sanitize(c, base, d1)`:
```cpp
return_trace (sanitize_shallow (c, base) &&
              (this->is_null () ||
               StructAtOffset<Type> (base, *this).sanitize (c, d1) ||
               neuter (c)));
```

`sanitize_shallow(c, base)`:
```cpp
if (unlikely (!c->check_struct (this))) return_trace (false);
if (unlikely (this->is_null ())) return_trace (true);
if (unlikely (!c->check_range (base, *this))) return_trace (false);
return_trace (true);
```

`check_struct(this)` checks the map offset field (4 bytes at file offset 8). This is within the buffer. Passes.

`is_null()` reads the map offset value (0x20202020). Within buffer. Not null.

`check_range(base, *this)` = `check_range(this, 0x20202020)`. `base` = `this` (ResourceForkHeader at offset 4). `check_range(offset 4, 0x20202020)` fails.

So `sanitize_shallow` returns false. So `map.sanitize` returns false.

So the crash must be in `check_struct(this)` in `ResourceForkHeader::sanitize` OR in the evaluation of `&(this+data)`.

Wait, let me reconsider `&(this+data)`. `this + data` calls `data(this)`. `data(this)` calls `is_null()` on the data offset. The data offset field is at file offset 4. `is_null()` reads the 4-byte value at offset 4 = 256. This is within the buffer. So no crash.
